channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Lula dá entrevista ao “Sem Censura”, da EBC, na 6ª feira
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will give an interview to EBC's 'Sem Censura' program this Friday (May 21, 2026) at 4 PM in Rio de Janeiro, hosted by Cissa Guimarães with guests Nath Finanças, Luciana Barreto, and Muka. Later that evening, he is expected to attend the inauguration of his cardiologist, Roberto Kalil Filho, at the ANM. On Saturday (April 23), he will inaugurate the CDTS headquarters of Fiocruz in Manguinhos.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro nega ter pedido encontro com Donald Trump
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro denied requesting a meeting with Donald Trump, stating any encounter would depend on an invitation from the White House. He said his team indicated a possible meeting next week, but the U.S. government has not confirmed it. Flávio also mocked Lula for not speaking English, emphasizing that the meeting’s details are solely up to Washington.

item.title: Governo quer fim da escala 6×1 aprovado na reta final da campanha
item.description: The Lula government is negotiating with Congress to approve the abolition of the 6×1 work schedule, aiming for the measure to take effect in September or October 2026, shortly before the elections. The strategy seeks to advance the labor reform’s impact to influence voters during the campaign.

item.title: ‘Se for culpado, tem de pagar exemplarmente’, diz Ciro Nogueira sobre Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Senator Ciro Nogueira (PP-PI) stated that Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) must be seriously and impartially investigated regarding his ties to Daniel Vorcaro, owner of Banco Master, and that if found guilty, he should be punished exemplarily under the law. He emphasized that no one should be shielded by political protection and that innocence must also be acknowledged. Nogueira, a target of Operation Compliance Zero, denied defending or accusing Flávio, insisting only on the need for impartial justice.

item.title: Nunes Marques amplia efetivo do TSE para julgar ações sobre propaganda irregular
item.description: TSE President Minister Nunes Marques has decided to increase the number of magistrates responsible for judging electoral propaganda irregularities, anticipating an early overload due to the premature intensification of the Lula-Bolsonaro rivalry. Besides Minister Estela Aranha, who already rapporteurs over 80 such cases, Marques and Vice President André Mendonça will also share rapporteurship duties. The move aims to ensure timely adjudication of electoral cases before the official campaign period begins.

item.title: Fim da escala 6x1 deve ter prazo para entrar em vigor caso PEC seja aprovada
item.description: The PEC proposing the end of the 6x1 work scale and reduction of the weekly workweek from 44 to 40 hours will include a transition period of 60, 90, or 120 days after promulgation, potentially taking effect during the electoral period. The text also discusses gradual implementation over two or three years, aiming to reduce employer costs by excluding certain charges on reduced hours. The proposal is a key electoral banner for Lula’s 2026 re-election bid, with the rapporteur’s report expected to be finalized by Monday.

item.title: Dino abre divergência e vota para derrubar anistia a partidos que descumpriram cota racial
item.description: Minister Flávio Dino voted to overturn the amnesty for political parties that failed to meet racial quotas in the 2022 elections, calling the pardon of sanctions a social setback. He filed a dissent in the STF’s virtual plenary judgment reviewing the constitutionality of the amendment that forgives parties for not allocating resources to Black and female candidatures. Relator Cristiano Zanin and Dias Toffoli support the amendment, stating the 30% resource floor is an unprecedented advancement in affirmative action policies.

item.title: ‘Queremos ver o Vorcaro falando’, diz Valdemar sobre CPI do Master
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto, president of the PL, advocated for the installation of a CPMI to investigate Banco Master and stated that the party supports the testimony of banker Daniel Vorcaro, whose deposition to the Federal Police is not public. Despite an audio leak by The Intercept Brasil showing Flávio Bolsonaro requesting funds from Vorcaro to finish the film 'Dark Horse', Valdemar reiterated that Flávio's presidential candidacy remains intact and that the party is focused on his pre-campaign, denying any deadline for deciding on his electoral viability.

item.title: Após esconder relação com Vorcaro, Flávio Bolsonaro diz que não tem 'nada a esconder'; VÍDEO
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro admitted to publicly hiding his contact with Daniel Vorcaro, citing a confidentiality clause tied to the financing of the film 'Dark Horse'. During a congressional session, he advocated for a CPMI to investigate Banco Master and claimed he has 'nothing to hide', despite previously denying any relationship with the imprisoned banker.

item.title: Ciro Nogueira diz que Flávio “tem que ser investigado”
item.description: Senator Ciro Nogueira (PP-PI) stated that Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for president and fellow party member, 'must be investigated' in the Banco Master case, refraining from taking sides despite both being under investigation. The comment was made in an interview with TV Clube on Thursday, the 21st, following new developments in the case after the release of messages.

item.title: PL aciona TSE contra Lula por uso da máquina e cita precedente da condenação de Bolsonaro
item.description: The PL party filed a representation with the TSE against President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, alleging improper use of public resources for personal political promotion through institutional events and official government channels. The party cites the 2022 conviction of Jair Bolsonaro for abuse of political power and misuse of state apparatus as a precedent. The action was filed on May 21, 2026.

item.title: ‘Não atinge minha honra’, diz Aldo Rebelo ao contestar expulsão do DC
item.description: Former minister Aldo Rebelo challenged a potential expulsion from the Christian Democracy (DC) party, initiated by party president João Caldas, who is promoting Joaquim Barbosa as the party’s 2026 presidential candidate. Rebelo argues the disciplinary process lacks factual basis, violates party statute, and should be decided by the party convention. The conflict has caused a party split, with state leaders opposing Barbosa and Paulo Cesar Quartiero withdrawing his gubernatorial bid in Roraima.

item.title: Aldo desafia cúpula do DC após processo de expulsão
item.description: Former Chamber of Deputies president Aldo Rebelo rejected the disciplinary process initiated by the Christian Democracy party to expel him, stating the move 'does not reach' his honor and calling it unfounded. He defended his political trajectory and questioned the legitimacy of the party's internal procedure.

item.title: Republicanos em MG cogita Cleitinho para disputa presidencial após desgaste de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The Republicans party in Minas Gerais is considering Senator Cleitinho as a potential presidential candidate for 2026 amid the image wear of Flávio Bolsonaro due to his ties with banker Daniel Vorcaro. Although Cleitinho leads polls for the Minas Gerais gubernatorial race, he has not yet decided his candidacy, stating he will make a decision by June based on personal and family matters. The party also leaves open the possibility of a PL alliance in Minas if Cleitinho runs for state office, aiming to unite the right.

item.title: 'Se for culpado, tem que pagar exemplarmente', diz Ciro Nogueira sobre Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Senator Ciro Nogueira (PP-PI) avoided defending or accusing Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) in the Banco Master investigation, stating that if guilty, he must pay exemplarily, and emphasizing the need for impartial investigations. He also denounced an alleged 'selective leak' in the media favoring the left and harming the right, noting the lack of coverage on scandals in Bahia involving government allies.

item.title: Petista aciona MP e TSE e pede investigação sobre financiamento de 'Dark Horse'
item.description: Federal deputy Arlindo Chinaglia (PT-SP) filed a representation with the Electoral Public Ministry and the TSE to investigate the alleged undisclosed million-dollar financing of the film 'Dark Horse', which he claims may violate electoral legislation. He argues the film could be functioning as a disguised campaign tool benefiting unidentified candidates. The request aims to determine whether illegal resources are being used to support candidacies in the 2026 elections.

item.title: Nova lei impõe execução imediata de medidas protetivas cíveis para mulheres
item.description: The new Law 15.412/2024, signed by Lula, mandates the immediate execution of civil protective measures for women victims of violence, removing the requirement for the victim to file a lawsuit. The law updates the Maria da Penha Law by removing references to the 1973 Code of Civil Procedure and aligning it with the 2015 CPC, enhancing the effectiveness of judicial protection orders in family, patrimonial, and domestic spheres.

item.title: Lula diz que aprendeu a falar “I love you” para dizer a Janja
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva joked that, despite not speaking English, he learned to say 'I love you' to communicate with First Lady Janja during a cultural announcement ceremony in Espírito Santo. He recalled his participation in the 2003 G8 summit, emphasizing his working-class roots and arguing that global leaders should learn from him, not the other way around, which earned him international respect.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro não assinou três das cinco CPIs sobre o Master que poderia apoiar
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) failed to sign three of the five available Senate CPI requests investigating Banco Master, including one from his ally Eduardo Girão and two from government-aligned senators, despite claiming he had signed all. He only supported requests from Carlos Jordy (PL-RJ) and Carlos Viana (PSD-MG), the latter still not filed. The contradiction between his statements and actions emerged after leaked messages showed him requesting money from Master’s owner, Daniel Vorcaro, to finance a film about Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: Planalto monitora Flávio nos EUA após visita bem-sucedida de Lula
item.description: The Brazilian government is monitoring with caution the possible meeting between Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and U.S. President Donald Trump in the United States, noting there is no official confirmation from Washington or Itamaraty. The Planalto views the initiative with reservations, fearing it could interfere in the diplomatic progress achieved after Lula’s successful May visit to the White House, which focused on resuming trade talks and reducing bilateral tensions. The administration aims to preserve the political capital gained from Lula’s visit, which strengthens his image as a capable negotiator and supports his 2026 electoral strategy.

item.title: Deputados pedem mobilização para garantir que escala 6x1 seja extinta ainda neste ano
item.description: Deputados and ministers state that the bill to end the 6x1 work scale will be voted on by Thursday, the 27th, reducing the weekly workload to 40 hours with two days off and no salary cut, while strengthening collective bargaining. Rapporteur Leo Prates (Republicanos-BA) will deliver the text on Monday and calls for worker mobilization to secure the 308 votes needed in the Chamber. Bill author Reginaldo Lopes (PT-MG) notes that two-thirds of Brazilians already work under the 5x2 scale and that those working 44 hours earn R$31,500 less annually, according to Ipea and Dieese.

item.title: Governo vai liberar Desenrola para adimplentes até junho, diz ministro
item.description: The federal government will launch by June 2026 a new phase of the Desenrola program targeting individuals who are current on their debts, lasting 90 days. Announced by Finance Minister Dario Durigan, the initiative will allow swapping high-interest debts for lower-rate credit, backed by the FGO fund, and will be implemented before the electoral period.

item.title: Câmara aprova projeto que proíbe sigilo sobre gastos públicos
item.description: The Chamber of Deputados approved a bill banning secrecy over public spending by authorities, including expenses for travel, lodging, and meals, making such data mandatorily transparent. The proposal amends the Access to Information Law, classifying intentional concealment as administrative impropriety and a responsibility crime, with automatic declassification after 120 days of inaction by the Mista Commission.

item.title: As violências legitimadas
item.description: Marilena Chauí's essay 'Brazil: Founding Myth and Authoritarian Society,' reissued in 2026, examines the roots of social and political authoritarianism in Brazil, criticizing the tendency to interpret the country through external parameters rather than its historical reality. The philosopher argues that this perspective leads to viewing the State as the sole effective agent, due to the absence of social classes capable of representing historical interests. Originally written during Fernando Henrique Cardoso's government, the work remains relevant for understanding authoritarian structures in Brazilian society.

item.title: Lula diz temer invasão de Trump à Amazônia e reclama de ‘fronteiras desguarnecidas’
item.description: President Lula warned that Donald Trump might attempt to invade or annex the Amazon, citing Trump's past claims over Greenland, Canada, and the Panama Canal. He argued that Brazil's borders are undermanned and vulnerable to invasion, calling for stronger national security measures. Despite these concerns, Lula said he sought to avoid war with the U.S. during his White House meeting, proposing a 'narrative war' to demonstrate Brazil's correctness on key issues.

item.title: Mario Frias diz a Flávio Dino que chega ao Brasil no dia 25 de maio
item.description: Federal deputy Mario Frias (PL-SP) announced he will return to Brazil on May 25 to make himself available to Minister Flávio Dino of the STF, after being summoned to clarify alleged irregularities in amendments allocated to the producer of the film 'Dark Horse', which depicts Jair Bolsonaro's trajectory. Frias had been on an international mission in the U.S. and had not been located by court officials in prior diligences. The case is tied to messages revealed by The Intercept Brasil showing his communication with Daniel Vorcaro, founder of Banco Master, regarding support for the film project.

item.title: Qual é a organização que levou Mário Frias para os EUA
item.description: Federal deputy Mário Frias (PL-SP) was taken to the United States by the organization Yes Brazil USA, a Florida-registered nonprofit that serves as a bridge between Brazilian politicians and the conservative community abroad. The trip, classified as an official mission, occurred amid investigations into the allocation of parliamentary amendments to organizations linked to the film 'Dark Horse' and has drawn scrutiny from the Supreme Federal Court regarding its authorization and costs.

item.title: ‘A candidatura de Flávio está mantida’, diz Valdemar após crise com Vorcaro
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto, president of the PL party, confirmed that Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential candidacy remains intact despite controversy over his request for funds from banker Daniel Vorcaro for the 'Dark Horse' film. He denied that the party set a 15-day deadline to decide on the candidacy’s viability, stating the period is for assessing poll performance and strengthening the pre-campaign. Valdemar emphasized Flávio’s early surge in polls, party unity, and dismissed concerns that right-wing voters might shift to candidates like Zema or Caiado.

item.title: Lula diz que Brasil precisa reforçar segurança para proteger Amazônia e cita falas de Trump
item.description: Lula said Brazil must strengthen its security and territorial protection due to international threats, citing Trump’s remarks about Greenland, Canada, and the Panama Canal as examples of risks to sovereignty. He warned that without preparedness, any country could attempt to invade the Amazon, and advocated for a 'narrative war' with the U.S., not direct confrontation. The comments come amid government concerns over the potential U.S. designation of Brazilian criminal factions as terrorist organizations.

item.title: Áudio: Parlamentares cobram CPMI do Banco Master durante sessão do Congresso
item.description: Lawmakers including Flávio Bolsonaro and Eduardo Girão called for a mixed parliamentary inquiry (CPMI) to investigate Banco Master during a congressional session, but President Davi Alcolumbre did not read the request, citing procedural discretion.

item.title: Lula usa Gaza para falar de “terra arrasada” deixada por Bolsonaro
item.description: President Lula compared the destruction of Gaza by Israeli forces to the alleged 'scorched earth' left by Jair Bolsonaro’s government, accusing him of dismantling public policies and governing through a 'hate cabinet'. He used the rhetoric of reconstruction to advocate for restoring social programs in Brazil, also criticizing disinformation and political violence attributed to his opponents.

item.title: STF autoriza INAC a participar de ação sobre mudanças na Lei da Ficha Limpa
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court (STF) admitted the Instituto Não Aceito Corrupção (INAC) as amicus curiae in the direct action of unconstitutionality challenging the amendments to the Clean Record Law, recognizing the institute’s institutional relevance in the fight against corruption. INAC will argue that the changes are unconstitutional, claiming they weaken eligibility rules and allow retroactive benefits for convicted individuals, constituting a setback for electoral integrity and public ethics. The action, filed by the Rede Sustentabilidade party, begins judgment this Friday in the Court’s virtual plenary.

item.title: O motivo apontado por integrante do PL para a versão de Flávio sobre Vorcaro
item.description: Federal Deputy Coronel Chrisóstomo (PL-RO) stated that Senator Flávio Bolsonaro’s initial denial of his relationship with former banker Daniel Vorcaro was an attempt to keep a private matter confidential, related to a film project about Jair Bolsonaro. After the audio was leaked by The Intercept, Flávio admitted the contact, but Chrisóstomo emphasized the discussion was personal and did not involve public funds. The PL party concluded the incident does not harm Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential pre-candidacy.

item.title: Alcolumbre diz que 'não pode responder' a perguntas sobre relação de Flávio com Vorcaro, CPI do Master e Messias
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre refused to answer four questions regarding the possible re-nomination of Jorge Messias to the STF, the installation of a mixed CPI to investigate the Master bank scandal, his failure to read the CPI request, and Flávio Bolsonaro’s ties to former banker Daniel Vorcaro. He also stated he will decide the legislative path for a bill granting benefits to political parties, still pending arrival from the Chamber, and named Senator Marcelo Castro as a potential rapporteur.

item.title: Congresso derruba veto de Lula e libera doação de bens durante campanha eleitoral
item.description: Congress overturned four vetoes by President Lula on the 2026 Budget Guidelines Law, including provisions allowing public asset donations in the three months before elections, federal funds for municipalities in default with up to 65,000 inhabitants, and federal resources for state and municipal roads and waterways. The vote to override the veto on defaulting municipalities was the most lopsided: 500 in favor, 22 against.

item.title: O que levou o PT a se ausentar de debate sobre a redução de maioridade penal na CCJ
item.description: The PT caucus absented itself from the CCJ session debating the PEC to lower the age of criminal responsibility, leaving deputy Talíria Petrone (Psol) alone in obstruction. The absence was decided in a prior caucus meeting, with the claim that only a view request was on the agenda, not the constitutional analysis. PT lawmakers labeled the issue an 'electoral bomb,' fearing that supporting the measure could alienate centrist and undecided voters who are sympathetic to the proposal.

item.title: Ligação de Flávio Bolsonaro com Vorcaro resgata Lula e outras fênix
item.description: Revelations about Senator Flávio Bolsonaro's connection to banker Daniel Vorcaro — including an audio in which he demands money and a visit while Vorcaro wore an electronic ankle monitor — triggered strong backlash and caused a drop of over five points in voting intentions, according to an Atlas poll. This episode reinforces the narrative of Lula as a political figure capable of rising from adversity, following past defeats, scandals, and imprisonment, positioning him once again as a symbol of resilience. Flávio’s allies acknowledge the damage to his campaign and are awaiting proof to sustain support, while the full impact on future polls remains uncertain.

item.title: Congresso derruba veto de Lula e libera emenda para dar trator, cesta básica e dinheiro nas eleições
item.description: Brazil's Congress overturned President Lula's veto that prohibited public donations of goods, money, and benefits during the 2026 electoral period, allowing distributions of tractors, food baskets, and funds via parliamentary amendments, provided there is a counterparty. The measure also enables transfers for state and municipal roads and waterways, and waives fiscal compliance requirements for small municipalities to sign agreements during the campaign. Lula had vetoed the provision as unconstitutional and against public interest, but Congress, led by Davi Alcolumbre, reinstated it in the 2026 Budget Guidelines Law (LDO).

item.title: Com vetos derrubados, cerca de 3 mil municípios inadimplentes poderão receber recursos
item.description: The National Congress restored four vetoed provisions in the 2026 Budget Guidelines Law (LDO), enabling around 3,000 municipalities with up to 65,000 inhabitants and fiscal arrears to sign agreements with the federal government and access funds from federal programs and parliamentary amendments. The decision also reinstated the possibility of public donations during the electoral period under donor-defined conditions and authorized federal funding for state and municipal roads and the Brazilian waterway system. Congress President Davi Alcolumbre emphasized the urgency of the measure to support small municipalities facing budgetary and fiscal challenges, particularly given the electoral blackout period under Law 9.504/1997 that restricts voluntary transfers in the three months before elections.

item.title: Ano eleitoral exige cautela: veja como investidores podem proteger o patrimônio
item.description: Election years increase financial market volatility in Brazil, demanding higher risk premiums from investors. Diversification, including international exposure and fixed income, is recommended as a patrimonial protection strategy, while defensive sectors in variable income are favored during political instability.

item.title: Lula cita Groenlândia e diz que Trump pode querer tomar Amazônia
item.description: Lula da Silva warned that Donald Trump's expansionist remarks about territories such as Greenland, Canada, and the Panama Canal signal a risk to the Amazon, advocating for increased investment in national defense and sovereignty due to Brazil's strategic resources. He criticized Bolsonaro's administration for destroying public policies and governing through a 'hate cabinet', while stating the US has accumulated a $415 billion trade surplus with Brazil over the last 15 years.

item.title: Congresso derruba veto de Lula e flexibiliza repasses a municípios em período eleitoral
item.description: Brazil's Congress overturned President Lula's vetoes to the 2026 Budget Guidelines Law (LDO), loosening rules on federal transfers to municipalities during the electoral period, including allowing donations and reinstating agreements for municipalities with up to 65,000 inhabitants that are in arrears. The move was backed by the government coalition, despite the PT's opposition to donation releases over concerns of 'vote-buying,' and included permission for allied deputies to vote in favor. Congress President Davi Alcolumbre stated the decision responds to mayors seeking resources for their cities.

item.title: Tebet diz que Flávio Bolsonaro seria “facilmente derrotado” por Lula
item.description: Former minister Simone Tebet (PSB) said she hopes Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) will be Lula’s opponent in the 2026 presidential runoff, claiming he would be 'easily defeated'. She cited multiple allegations against the senator, including the 'rachadinhas' salary scheme in the Rio de Janeiro State Assembly, the purchase of a Brasília mansion financed by BRB, and suspicious financial movements in a Rio chocolate franchise, all of which, she argued, require clarification.

item.title: Congresso derruba veto que proibia repasses a municípios inadimplentes
item.description: Congress overrode four presidential vetoes to the 2026 Budget Guidelines Law (LDO), allowing federal funds and in-kind donations to flow to municipalities with up to 65,000 inhabitants even if they are in debt (CAUC list), and authorizing federal resources for state/municipal roads and waterway improvements. The changes benefit mayors in an election year by enabling legislators to direct funds to their electoral bases without federal obstruction.

item.title: Congresso derruba veto de Lula e libera repasses a municípios inadimplentes
item.description: Brazil's National Congress overruled President Lula's veto of the 2026 Budget Guidelines Law (LDO), allowing federal funds to be released to municipalities with up to 65,000 inhabitants that are in arrears. The decision was made in a joint session called by Congress President Davi Alcolumbre, reversing restrictions that had barred these municipalities from receiving federal resources and signing agreements with the Union.

item.title: Rebelo mantém candidatura e diz que Barbosa é nome “clandestino”
item.description: Aldo Rebelo maintains his presidential pre-candidacy, calling Joaquim Barbosa's nomination a 'clandestine' move lacking party support after National DC President João Caldas announced Barbosa as the new candidate, despite Rebelo's official launch in February. Rebelo claims he was not informed, calls the action incorrect, and threatens legal action if obstacles arise, insisting the candidate must be chosen at a party convention, not by unilateral decision. He also mocked Barbosa's failed 2018 PSB bid and noted his 0.2% polling in the Atlas/Bloomberg survey, which Caldas labeled a 'logical' reason for the change.

item.title: Congresso derruba quatro vetos à LDO de 2026 e libera repasses a municípios
item.description: Congress overrode four presidential vetoes on the 2026 Budget Guidelines Law (LDO), allowing federal funds to finance state and municipal roadworks, Brazilian waterway expenditures, electoral-period donations, and agreements with small municipalities without requiring fiscal compliance. The executive branch argued the measures were unconstitutional, but lawmakers like Bia Kicis supported the overrides as beneficial to the public, while Chico Alencar warned that electoral donations could enable vote-buying.

item.title: Parlamentares contrariam consultorias do Congresso, derrubam veto e liberam doações a municípios no período eleitoral
item.description: Congress overturned the presidential veto on the 2026 Budget Guidelines Law (LDO), allowing public donations to municipalities during the electoral period if there is a counterparty obligation. The move went against the technical advice of congressional consultancies, which warned it violates electoral law by enabling public resource use to favor candidates. The executive had vetoed the LDO, arguing temporary laws cannot create exceptions to permanent norms like electoral legislation.

item.title: Lula diz que Brasil precisa resolver “problema de segurança”
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated that Brazil must resolve its 'security problem', emphasizing the need to strengthen border and Amazon protection, citing the country's vast territory and strategic natural resources. He criticized the perception of being defenseless and referenced Donald Trump's remarks about Greenland and Canada to warn of potential threats to Brazilian sovereignty in the Amazon.

item.title: Malandragem de deputados tenta fazer o público de mané
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies once again prioritizes its own interests while the public is distracted by recurring scandals. The practice of legislating for legislators' benefit repeats itself using the same old method, exploiting societal inattention.
